inspiration.observed_pattern: A query converts a delimited numeric string into JSON_TABLE rows with FOR ORDINALITY, computes adjacent differences with partitioned LAG, groups the differences into minimum and maximum bounds, and filters or classifies sequences by allowable step ranges.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Reauthored as a sensor-batch delta audit. Space-delimited readings are expanded into typed rows, adjacent readings are compared per batch, grouped extrema classify ascending, descending, mixed, and single-reading batches, and the final report is ordered by batch ID. The source table, data format values, labels, and puzzle context are not copied.

fixture_notes: Two batches have uniformly ascending or descending steps within the allowed range, one has an out-of-range step, and one has only a single reading with no delta. The report exposes all four classifications.
determinism_notes: Batch IDs, names, space-delimited readings, JSON_TABLE ordinality, step bounds, and final ordering are fixed. No clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE sensor_reading_batches (batch_id INT PRIMARY KEY, batch_name VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL, readings_csv VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL)

steps.sql: WITH reading_deltas AS (SELECT batches.batch_id, batches.batch_name, jt.position, jt.reading - LAG(jt.reading) OVER (PARTITION BY batches.batch_id ORDER BY jt.position) AS step_delta FROM sensor_reading_batches AS batches INNER JOIN JSON_TABLE(CONCAT('[', REPLACE(batches.readings_csv, ' ', ','), ']'), '$' COLUMNS (NESTED PATH '$[*]' COLUMNS (position FOR ORDINALITY, reading INT PATH '$'))) AS jt ON TRUE), grouped_bounds AS (SELECT batch_id, batch_name, COUNT(step_delta) AS measured_steps, MIN(step_delta) AS minimum_step, MAX(step_delta) AS maximum_step FROM reading_deltas GROUP BY batch_id, batch_name) SELECT batch_id, batch_name, measured_steps, minimum_step, maximum_step, CASE WHEN measured_steps = 0 THEN 'insufficient' WHEN minimum_step >= 1 AND maximum_step <= 3 THEN 'steady_up' WHEN minimum_step >= -3 AND maximum_step <= -1 THEN 'steady_down' ELSE 'mixed' END AS batch_class FROM grouped_bounds ORDER BY batch_id

checks.sql: SELECT batch_id, batch_name, readings_csv FROM sensor_reading_batches ORDER BY batch_id
